messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are cracking—more than we’ve seen in years. Even the usual watchdogs are looking the other way, and the air smells like something’s coming. Let’s keep our heads down but stay ready—this could go fast."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are cracking—even the tea house is louder than the state radio these days. Late paychecks, empty promises, and generals who can’t even keep their own courts in line? Something’s coming, but no one’s sure if it’s a collapse or just another show. Keep your ears open, but don’t trust the script—this time, the whispers might be the only honest thing left."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting they feel it too. The usual signs are there, but the silence around them is louder than the noise. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are cracking—people are talking louder than they should, and even the ones who used to enforce silence are hesitating. The regime’s still standing, but it’s like a house with the foundation shifting—you can feel it in the way the floors creak underfoot. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The question isn’t *if*, but *when* and *how*."*"
Sender 5: "*"The ship’s drifting—no one’s at the wheel, and the crew’s starting to notice. Payments are still coming, but the rest? The cracks are showing, even in places you wouldn’t expect. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let anyone see you looking too closely."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are cracking—everyone can see it now. The question isn’t *if* things will break, but *when* and *how hard* we’ll need to push when they do. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your hands ready."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s admitting they feel it too. The usual signs are all there, even the ones they can’t hide: the money men are nervous, the soldiers are restless, and the women in the market aren’t even pretending to be afraid anymore. We’re not there yet, but the question isn’t *if*—it’s how hard the fall will be when it comes."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who’ve always had one foot out the door are suddenly in a hurry. But the real question isn’t if, it’s when, and whether the generals will step in before the whole thing collapses on itself. Keep your heads down, but don’t pack *too* light—just in case."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are cracking—even the ones who used to whisper in the dark are now shouting at each other, and the guards are packing their bags. The question isn’t if, but how fast, and whether the streets will move before the guns do. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to trip over our own feet."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are cracking—even the taxis are talking like it’s a matter of when, not if. The banks are tightening, the courts are breaking, and the regime’s own people are asking *us* what we’ve heard. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are cracking—fast. The usual signs are all there, but the timing is what’s terrifying: the bank’s flailing, the soldiers are talking, and even the censors are slipping. If the foreigners are asking questions *now*, we’re closer than we think. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we need to know which way the guns will swing."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s saying it out loud yet. The ship’s drifting, and the crew’s either too scared or too busy watching their own backs to notice. Stay sharp, but don’t let it show."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are cracking—even the shopkeepers are talking like it’s inevitable now. But the guards still march in step, and the foreign guests are coming. Either the show’s almost over, or they’re setting a trap. Either way, we should be ready for the moment the music stops."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are cracking—even the kids in the streets know it now. The question isn’t *if* things will break, but *when*, and whether we’ll be ready."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are cracking—even the usual whispers are now open talk, and the regime’s denials sound like they’re reading from a script no one’s watching anymore. The question isn’t *if* things are breaking, but how fast—and whether they’ll try to burn it all down before they go."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are cracking—even the taxi drivers are saying what we’ve all been thinking. The regime’s grip is slipping, but we need to be smart about how we move. Let’s talk in person soon—somewhere quiet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are cracking—small signs, but too many to ignore. Meet at the usual spot tomorrow, but let’s keep it quiet; even the air feels like it’s listening now."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are cracking—even the taxi drivers are saying what we’ve all been thinking. But we still don’t know if the rot goes all the way down or if this is just a trap to see who’s listening. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and keep your eyes open."*"
Sender 19: "*"The ship is drifting—no one’s at the helm, and the crew’s already packing their bags. The market’s quiet, but the whispers aren’t. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t a drill."*"
Sender 20: "*"The ship’s drifting—no one’s at the wheel, and the crew’s starting to notice. The real question now isn’t *if* things break, but *when* and how hard they’ll land. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re not the only ones watching."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s saying it out loud. The usual cracks are widening, and the ones in charge are moving pieces we can’t see yet. Stay sharp, but don’t let it show."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are cracking—elites aren’t talking, the ranks are restless, and even the censors are slipping. The system’s still running, but it’s running on fumes. Keep your ears open, your plans quiet, and your bags packed—just in case."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are cracking—elites are settling scores, the banks are emptying, and even the foreign airlines are preparing for something. We’ve all seen the signs, but this isn’t just nerves—it’s the sound of the machine breaking down. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. We’ll know soon enough if the guards will still follow orders."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first tremors. My cousin’s silence, the general’s words, even the way the embassies are suddenly moving slower—it’s all adding up, but the question is whether the regime’s falling apart or just testing how far it can push before we react. Stay sharp, but keep your heads down."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are cracking—more than we thought. The soldiers at the checkpoint near the market were laughing with the bakers yesterday, and the black market’s acting like the regime’s already out of bullets. Keep your heads down, but be ready—this isn’t just a storm, it’s the calm before something else. And watch your phones."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
